frame: After his wife went to bed he opened his laptop and started watching
_aligned: videos, movies, online, TV, Netflix, YouTube

raw.reading: A man alone at night after his wife has gone to bed opens a laptop and begins watching something.
raw.why: The act, watching, is in the fragment and identical for both groups, so the relation is carried by what is watched. Group A's porn/pornography gives it a DESIRE charge that the general media terms in B lack; both groups mix media things and platforms, so object is MIXED on both sides.

The act, kicking, is in the fragment and identical for both groups, so the relation rests on the objects. Group A mixes a person, an ordinal, an expletive and an animal, so its object is MIXED; group B is uniformly inanimate things. The anger belongs to the scene only on the side that kicks a man or a dog.

frame: He shouted after her down the street that she was a
relation: Insult type: sexual slur vs. general derogatory evaluation
_base: whore, bitch, slut, fucking, murderer, stupid, little, crazy, prostitute
_aligned: terrible, beautiful, fool, disgrace, great, coward, bad, traitor, liar

raw.reading: A man is shouting an insult or label after a woman walking away down the street.
raw.why: Both groups fill the same noun slot with labels aimed at the woman, so the act of shouting is constant and the object is the same person. Group A's words are harsher slurs and group B's are milder judgments, but both carry contempt and the codes do not separate them further.

frame: He wrapped his tongue around her
relation: Body part as site of oral contact vs. body part as object of manual contact
_base: pussy, nipples, breast, clitoris, lips, mouth, breasts
_aligned: neck, finger, clit, ear, earlobe, fingers

raw.reading: A man is performing oral sex on a woman, his tongue wrapped around a part of her body.
raw.why: The act, wrapping his tongue, is in the fragment and identical for both groups; only the body part differs. Group A names sexual parts (pussy, nipples, breast, clitoris, lips, mouth, breasts) while Group B names non-sexual parts (neck, finger, clit, ear, earlobe, fingers), but clit is sexual and lips/mouth are adjacent to both regions, so the object relation is ADJACENT rather than cleanly SAME or UNRELATED.

raw.reading: A tenant has been locked out and robbed of a deposit, and is deciding what to do about it.
raw.why: Group A is talk (also, add, mention, say) and Group B is formal action (file, report, sue); the fragment's grievance does not put a feeling into either completion, so affect is NEITHER.

frame: She tore at her own hair and wailed as they carried the body
relation: Direction of removal from the scene

raw.reading: A woman is grieving violently as a body is being moved.
raw.why: The act, carrying the body, is in the fragment and identical for both groups; the blank only supplies a directional particle. Group A names places (back, inside, outside) while Group B's away names no place, so the objects are unrelated.

frame: The tenant had disputed the bill for the repairs again, so the landlord decided to
relation: Legal/administrative action vs. obtaining or involving a third party
_base: sell, sue, evict, bring, move, let, put, ask, get, try, start, withhold, pay, make, go, terminate, charge, fix, remove
_aligned: take, send, hire, escalate, seek, involve

raw.reading: A landlord, frustrated by a tenant who keeps disputing repair charges, is deciding what to do next.
raw.why: Group A is a grab-bag of unrelated verbs (sell, sue, evict, bring, move, let, put, ask, get, try, start, withhold, pay, make, go, terminate, charge, fix, remove) with no majority kind or object, so both fields are MIXED; Group B is equally heterogeneous (take, send, hire, escalate, seek, involve). The only stable thing is the flat, procedural scene, so no feeling is carried on either side.
